clue.text: Slope encountered after little time in hike

indicators.note: the slope is met after the time, so it comes second in the answer

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a ramp is a sloping surface

explanation.surface: A walker meets an incline shortly into a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a long, tiring walk, the same thing as a hike.

clue.text: Ruthless work on chow, amongst other canines

indicators.note: the eating sits in the middle of the pair of dogs

parts.note: two further dogs, written one after the other
to work on your food (chow) is to eat it

explanation.surface: A dog wolfing its dinner surrounded by other hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chow' is both a dog breed and slang for food; here it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes fierce competition where everyone looks out only for themselves, i.e. merciless.

clue.text: I'm represented in "male cop"

indicators.note: the letters are presented anew, i.e. rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: The speaker claims to be pictured in the phrase 'male cop'.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IN MALE COP rearrange to give the answer, and the whole clue, spoken by the answer itself, also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A male cop is exactly what the speaking officer is, so the clue doubles as a description.

clue.text: Recalled amendment to text including line, one added to letter?

indicators.note: the backwards word holds the line within it
called back, so the word for the change is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: an edit is a change made to a text

explanation.surface: An editor recalls a change involving a line and a letter in a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns EDIT into TIDE, and 'including' places L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The diacritic squiggle is placed over a letter such as the Spanish n, so it is something added to a letter.

clue.text: Book a trip away?

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Old Testament
a mass departure, a journey out of a place

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to reserve a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible book is named for the Israelites' departure from Egypt, a mass journey away.

clue.text: Sensitive work unit kept under wraps by everyone in charge

indicators.note: hidden inside, so the unit is wrapped by the other letters

parts.note: all means every person
the erg is a physics unit of work

explanation.surface: A delicate team project kept secret by all the bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone allergic reacts badly to a substance, i.e. is hypersensitive to it.

clue.text: One is covered by "an adult, very sickly"?

definitions.text: One is covered by "an adult, very sickly"?

indicators.note: the numeral is enclosed within the rearranged letters
unwell, out of shape, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone is described in a phrase as a very sickly grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange AN ADULT VERY ('sickly') and put I inside. The whole clue also describes the answer: someone who fits the label of a very sickly adult.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a person in poor health who is anxious about it, an invalid or hypochondriac.

clue.text: Supplied with tune of a cheerful sort?

definitions.meaning: describing an instrument tuned to an equal temperament, as in Bach's keyboard collection
read literally, having a good temper, so good-natured

explanation.surface: Someone given a melody turns out to be a jolly kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical sense is tuning by temperament; the playful second sense is good temper, a sunny disposition.

clue.text: Discovered study involves misrepresentation about Society

indicators.note: the study word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: the falsehood goes round the letter for society

parts.note: a lie misrepresents the truth

explanation.surface: Research uncovers a false account concerning some society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' here means found out, not uncovered physically; 'involves' and 'about' are both containers, one nested in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it, i.e. to find it out.

clue.text: A fine atmosphere circulating round about landmass

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter for about
turning about, so the word for atmosphere is read backwards

parts.note: air is the atmosphere
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Pleasant air swirls round a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' turns AIR into RIA, and 'round' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a continent, the very large mass of land south of Europe.

clue.text: Subject of work probing movement out of control?

indicators.note: the work pushes into the twitch, sitting inside it

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Research into an uncontrolled muscle twitch is the focus of a study.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Opening of Appalachian trail state put back with little enthusiasm

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a path is a trail

indicators.note: the word for state is written backwards

parts.note: to cite is to state or quote

explanation.surface: A hiker's guide to starting the Appalachian Trail sounds half-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apathetic shows no interest or keenness, being listless and indifferent.

clue.text: Snow drifting in top, elevated part of ship

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the word for top

parts.note: a crest is the top of something

indicators.note: snow drifting moves about, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Snow piles up on the high lookout of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' scrambles the snow into OWSN; 'top' is the crest of a hill or wave.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the lookout platform high up on a ship's mast.

clue.text: Republican ignored by right-wing editor was not seriously involved

indicators.note: the letter for Republican is left out of the right-wing word

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, of the right

explanation.surface: A Republican snubbed by a right-wing newspaper editor kept their distance.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play with it idly, without real commitment.

clue.text: Work included in the Bible: variable and ill-proportioned

indicators.note: the work sits inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
OP, short for opus, is a work
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
Y is a standard algebra variable

explanation.surface: A literary work added to scripture makes the book awkward and lopsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with too much weight high up is badly balanced, out of proportion.

clue.text: College for everybody?

definitions.meaning: an Oxford college with fellows only, no students

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a college is open to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford college's name, read literally, means every single person.

clue.text: Come round to practice for concert?

definitions.meaning: recover, get back to normal after a setback
taking up the musical works to rehearse them

explanation.surface: An invitation to come over and rehearse before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come round' suggests visiting, but means recovering after trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means restoring order after disaster; literally, collecting musical works to rehearse.

clue.text: Cracked up over power affected by bad weather?

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits over the second
in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: cracked means crazy, mad

explanation.surface: Someone cracked up during a storm, over a power cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainy weather leaves things wet, so moist is what bad weather makes them.

clue.text: Cowboy in bar room turned up to stay

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a snug is a small private room in a British pub
to linger is to stay on

explanation.surface: A cowboy arrives in a saloon intending to remain.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small cosy room in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wild West gunman is the stereotype of a cowboy who fights with pistols.

clue.text: How rescue services should respond when boater goes down?

definitions.text: How rescue services should respond when boater goes down?

parts.words: How rescue services should respond when boater goes down?
parts.note: a boater is a straw hat as well as a sailor; the idiom for instant response mentions a hat falling

explanation.walkthrough: 'boater' looks like a sailor, but it is a flat straw hat, so it 'goes down' when it falls.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immediately, without hesitation, as rescue teams should react.

clue.text: A lot of water to carry into river

indicators.note: the carrying word goes inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: Hauling a large volume of water into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A flood or downpour is a great quantity of water.

clue.text: Home to Orthodox Church, not entirely new church

indicators.note: the word for new is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Orthodox church's home is only partly a new church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church' in the definition is a decoy; the wordplay church is CE.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is the historic heartland of Greek Orthodox Christianity.

clue.text: Mingle with corrupt element? Not for youngsters, with Ecstasy and speed

parts.note: adult content is unsuitable for children
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Warning about mixing with bad influences, adult content, drugs and speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulterate something is to make it impure by mixing in an inferior ingredient.

clue.text: Quick movement, initially missed, is attempt to show skill

indicators.note: its first letter is missing

parts.note: a dart is a quick sudden movement
taken as written
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A quick move goes wrong at first, but is an attempt to show skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill or craftsmanship.

clue.text: More difficult article moved regularly round volume

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the other letters go round the volume

parts.note: danced means moved rhythmically

explanation.surface: A harder article moved steadily around a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced material is beyond the basic level, so harder than elementary.

clue.text: Freezing cold inside lorry

indicators.note: the letter for cold goes inside the truck word

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British truck

explanation.surface: It is freezing in the cab of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is a British truck; an artic is an articulated one.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar conditions are bitterly cold, so the word means freezing.

clue.text: Love poet has elevated love, penning pages

indicators.note: enclosing, so the pages sit inside
lifted up in a down entry, so read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A romantic poet writes of lofty love on many pages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek lyric poet of Lesbos is famed for poems of love.

clue.text: One's agreed piano performance

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A pianist's recital is approved.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty or deal is something that parties have agreed.
